lede: The biggest thing on the civic calendar this week is the San Miguel County BOCC sitting as the Housing Authority on August 19 — affordable housing compliance procedures are on the table at a moment when the finances are stretched thin, and there's also a public hearing on an insubstantial amendment worth watching. Alongside that, Telluride's P&Z takes its first formal look at school district employee housing on the TMHS site, HARC weighs preliminary review of the Shandoka Lot redevelopment, and Ouray County's Planning Commission holds three public hearings including a proposed repeal of an entire section of its land use code. Tuesday also marks the first day of school for Telluride R-1.

notable.stake: HARC decides whether to retroactively approve an unpermitted structure in the historic district.
Preliminary large-scale review of Shandoka Lot redevelopment — new construction on multiple buildings.
Commission recommends 2027 campground and shower fee increases, including a 25% shower rate jump.
BOCC reviews housing authority compliance and holds a public hearing on a land-use amendment.
Three public hearings: repeal of entire land use code section, SUP amendment, and exception application.
Public hearings on four special event liquor permits for upcoming Telluride events.
First formal review of school district employee housing proposal on the TMHS campus.
